bib.title: Why do Nearest Neighbor Language Models Work?
bib.venue: preprint (arXiv v2, 17 Jan 2023; PDF says 'Preprint. Under review.')

read.skipped: reference list skimmed; appendices read except the full tables of Appendices B/C

question: Why does kNN-LM improve perplexity over its base LM even when its datastore is the base LM's own training set?
hypothesis: The gain comes from identifiable design differences between kNN-LM and a parametric LM (input representation, datastore capacity, approximate search, temperature), not from extra data.
contributions: A generalised softmax formulation (Eq. 5) that exposes kNN-LM's design choices
Three main reasons kNN-LM works: a different input representation, approximate kNN search, softmax temperature
Several hypotheses ruled out, and a trainable-embedding alternative that recovers 55% of the gain without retrieval

method.summary: Re-implement kNN-LM on a 268M-parameter Transformer LM over WikiText-103 with BPE (33K vocab), generalise it as an interpolation of two softmaxes, and ablate one design choice at a time.

datasets.name: WikiText-103
datasets.size: nearly 150M BPE tokens in the training data; datastore 150M+ entries, about 300GB (fp16 293GB)
datasets.preprocessing: BPE vocabulary of 33K trained on the corpus

models.name: base LM
models.architecture: Transformer LM, modified from Baevski and Auli 2018

training.objective: cross-entropy; trainable embedding matrices Wds trained with other parameters fixed

inference.temperature: softmax temperature on the kNN distribution swept 0 to 3 at 0.1 steps
inference.retrieval: k=1024 nearest neighbours, FAISS approximate search vs exact; lambda tuned on dev and fixed at inference

metrics.name: perplexity
metrics.definition: base LM, interpolated, kNN-only and oracle (best lambda per token)

results.claim: The kNN-LM baseline lowers test perplexity of the 268M base LM from 21.750 to 19.174 (att, L2) and 19.095 (att, IP).
results.setup: WikiText-103, k=1024, datastore of all 150M training tokens
results.table: Table 1, rows Base LM and kNN-LM-L2 att

results.claim: The input representation matters: querying with the feed-forward output instead of the attention output leaves the kNN-LM at 20.734 (L2) and 21.101 (IP).
results.table: Table 1, rows kNN-LM-L2 ffn and kNN-LM-IP ffn
results.note: ffn+IP is the parametric model's own representation and similarity and is the worst variant

results.claim: A separate trainable V x D output matrix on the attention output, interpolated with the base LM, recovers about 55% of kNN-LM's gain with no retrieval.
results.setup: Learned Wds with att, interpolated perplexity 20.353 vs 19.095 for kNN-LM
results.quote: we can recover about 55% of the performance gain achieved by

results.claim: Approximate search beats exact search: FAISS mask and score give 19.174 vs 19.735 for the exact mask and exact score.
results.table: Table 3, rows FAISS mask FAISS score and real mask real score
results.note: about 2.6% relative improvement per the introduction

results.claim: The authors suggest approximate search acts as a regularizer against overfitting to a datastore built from the training set.
results.setup: hypothesis supported by token-level analysis (longer, higher-context-entropy words benefit more from approximate neighbours)
results.quote: We hypothesize that this is related to regularization for preventing overﬁtting

results.claim: Tuning the kNN softmax temperature matters: t=1 is only coincidentally near optimal in the original settings, and the gap between default and optimal can reach 3.7% relative perplexity.
results.setup: temperature swept 0 to 3, 5% subsampled and full datastore
results.quote: the relative perplexity gap between the default and optimal temperature can be as high as 3.7%

results.claim: A bigger datastore keeps helping almost linearly; even a 5% datastore (about 15GB) beats the base LM.
results.quote: Even with just 5% of the datastore size

results.claim: Simply giving each word type more trained embeddings (over-parameterising the softmax) is only about half as effective as kNN-LM and does not improve consistently with n.
results.setup: n embeddings per word type, Figure 3
results.quote: although only about half as effective as kNN-LM

results.claim: Ruled out: ensembling with another model, sparsification, memorisation, soft labels, stolen probabilities, optimising the interpolated loss.
results.quote: Probably Wrong Hypotheses for Why kNN-LMs Work

limits: One model family (268M Transformer), one dataset (WikiText-103), with a BPE vocabulary of 33K that gives a worse base perplexity than Khandelwal et al.'s 260K-vocabulary model; the authors argue relative gains are similar.
The datastore is the model's own training set; the paper explains why kNN-LM helps there, not how retrieval from fresh or external text helps.
The regularisation account of approximate search is a hypothesis; the authors present token-level correlations, not a causal test.
No confidence intervals or seeds are reported; perplexity only.
The 55% replacement still sits below kNN-LM and depends on combining two different layer views.
